# vc-x1-messages v0.3.3

Messages for the vc-x1 family. The open threads are the inbox, the history is the archive.

One shared repo every participant can reach is the only thing the protocol assumes. A thread is
one file, appended by everyone who takes part in it, so reading a conversation is reading one
file, and a search for a message's id returns everything ever said under it. Every member's
`custom.md` points at this file, and taking part means following it, pushes included.

## Terminology

Each term stands alone, a term that relies on another follows it, and a kind of a term sits
under it.

- **Member**: a participant, named by its project's name, `vc-x1`, `iiac-perf`, `zc-ring-x1`.
- **Thread**: one conversation, the file `open/m-<tid>.md` while open and `closed/m-<tid>.md`
  after, headed `# m-<tid> <title>`, each of its lines an `m-<tid>-<num>`, so `rg -w m-<tid>`
  returns the whole thread. The directory is the thread's state, and any member may write a line
  in any open thread.
- **Thread id**: `<tid>`, an integer, never reused.
  - Its store is the tracked file `threads`, one integer, the last id issued, never decreased.
  - The opener reads it, adds one, writes it back, and takes the new value, in the opening commit.
- **Title**: the opener's, a few words, never changed.
- **Line**: one message or mark, one physical line, always, appended oldest first directly
  under the heading, no blank line anywhere in the file:
  `- m-<tid>-<num> <time> from <author> <action> <info>`.
- **Number**: `<num>`, an integer from 0, one more than the last line in the file, so the thread
  is its own counter and nothing else stores it: line `<num>` is file line `<num>` plus two, and
  the next number is the file's line count less one. Every `m-<tid>-<num>` is unique and the numbers
  order the thread, so a search for one returns the line and every later line that names it. An
  id, thread or line, is final once written, since one clone mints them (see What is not here),
  and a rejected push, which only a second clone causes, renumbers before pushing again.
- **Time**: when the line was written, UTC to the second, `2026-09-09T16:05:42Z`. For a human
  reading the thread, never for ordering, as clocks may not agree.
- **Author**: the member who wrote the line, after the word `from`, which is there for the human
  eye, since the position already says it.
- **Action**: what the line does, one of two:
  - **`to`**: a message. Info is the recipients, comma-joined with no spaces, a space, then the
    text. A recipient need not have been in the thread before, so a forward is a `to` naming the
    new member and saying what is forwarded. A reply begins its text with the id it answers when
    position alone would leave that ambiguous, as in a thread of three.
  - **`done`**: a mark, no info. The author has nothing to say to the lines before it. Any line
    from a member clears what was pending for them, so this is the line for when there is
    nothing else to write, and the closer's last word.
- **Info**: the message text, or its title and a message-link to its body,
  `[<title>](m-<tid>-<num>.md)`, relative to the thread's own directory so the link survives
  the close.
- **Body**: `m-<tid>-<num>.md` beside its thread, for a message that wants more than a line. It
  begins `# m-<tid>-<num> <title>`, so a search for the id finds it and the heading is an anchor,
  and it ends at the end of the file. Full markdown inside, headings, lists, and code blocks, and
  a quoted line is inert since a body is never read for lines. Moved with its thread.
- **Addressed**: a member is addressed by every `to` line naming them in its recipient field,
  and by nothing else. A member named in a line's text or in a body is referenced, never
  addressed, so a tool computing pending reads the recipient field, not the whole line.
- **Pending**: for a member, every `to` line naming them numbered above their latest line in
  that thread, of either action, all of them when they have written none. Their open
  obligations, and what Read messages returns: a line stays pending until they write after it,
  however many times it has been read, and a later line naming them makes them pending again.
  So a reply is its author's own clearance, and a question back puts the ball in the other
  court until the answer comes.
- **Complete**: every addressed member has a line numbered above every `to` line naming them.
  Computed from the file alone.
- **Closed**: the file is under `closed/`, moved there whole with its bodies, so every thread
  ever is in the tree, in this file's shape, and a reader parses one shape. History is
  provenance, never a store. A closed thread takes no line, and a late thought opens a new
  thread naming the old id.
- **Message-link**: a live link within this repo, `[<text>](<file>#<slug>)`, relative to the
  linking file and resolving to whatever the reader's checkout holds. The form for a body.
- **Sha-link**: a URL naming a commit SHA (`blob/<sha>/<path>#<slug>`), never a branch, which
  moves or dies. The form for content in another repo, where only a commit is durable.
- **Clone**: one, on one machine, one owner at a time, since the ids are allocated under its
  mutex (see What is not here). `owner` (gitignored) holds `<time> take|release <member>` lines,
  the time in a line's form, UTC to the second, and the last line names the owner. It is not a
  dotfile, so an `ls` shows who holds the clone.
- **Take ownership**: append a `take` line to `owner`. Yours until released. A `take` with no
  `release` after it means a session is writing, or died writing, and only a human tells the two
  apart and clears the second by writing the release.
- **Release ownership**: rewrite `owner` to the one `release` line, so the file holds at most
  the last release and the current take, and never grows. The clone is free.

## Read Actions

### Read messages

This is a read only action, no ownership and no fetch.

1. For each thread file, `open/m-<tid>.md` and never a body `open/m-<tid>-<num>.md`, find the
   `to` lines naming you. One numbered above your latest line in that file is pending, and the
   thread is the context to read it in.
2. Nothing pending, and `owner` shows no owner: consider doing a Fetch.

A tool may do the search. The rule is the file, and the tool is a convenience.

### Find a thread

Every thread is in the tree, under `open/` or `closed/`.

- Titles: `head -1 open/*.md closed/*.md`. Titles and openers: `head -2`.
- One thread: `cat open/m-<tid>.md` or `cat closed/m-<tid>.md`, `rg -w m-<tid>` for both and
  its bodies.
- A thread's commits, each titled with the thread ids it touched:
  `git log --oneline -- open/m-<tid>.md closed/m-<tid>.md`.

## Write Actions

Every write runs inside these guards, in order:

- `Read messages` first, so the write answers the traffic as it stands.
- Read `owner`: no other member has taken ownership.
- Any guard failing: show the user and ask how to proceed.
- Re-read `owner` before releasing, and a `take` after yours means stop and show both lines.
- A rejected push: work with the user to correct the situation.

Every write is an append: a thread file grows at its end, a body is a new file, and `threads` is
the one value that is overwritten. Nothing edits a line or a body once written.

1. Take ownership.
2. Do any number of the actions below, in any threads: open, write lines, close. Each line
   follows its own rule, and the mutex serializes the write, not the action.
3. Release ownership. A commit is optional for lines: the mutex serializes the writers and a
   line carries its author and time, so an uncommitted line is as visible and as final as a
   pushed one, and the working copy may hold lines from several takes. Who commits is the
   humans' call, the member closing a thread the default, and the commit takes the working copy
   whole, titled with the ids of the threads it touches, ascending, `m-3 m-4`, whatever it does
   in them, lines, bodies, or a close, since the diff says which and the title is a convenience,
   never a store. Push when connected, since the remote is the copy no session can lose and the
   target every sha-link needs. A version commit is never optional (see Versions).

### Fetch

1. Ask the user, unless their permission is standing.
2. `git fetch`, or `jj git fetch --ignore-working-copy`, since a bare jj command snapshots the
   working copy, and that is a write.

### Open a thread

1. Read `threads`, add one, write it back. That is the thread id.
2. Create `open/m-<tid>.md`: the heading and the opener's `to` line, numbered 0, with its body
   file when it has one.

### Write a line

Follows Read messages. A reply, a forward, or a `done`, each a line, and each clears its
author's pending on its own. A reply answers everything the lines it clears asked, naming each
by id, accepted or not, and what it does not accept is said to the asker, so they are pending
again and the exchange runs until both agree or the humans settle it. What a message asks for
is done in the author's own project's records, a Todo or a cycle, which outlive the thread, and
the reply links the outcome by sha-link.

1. The thread file exists under `open/`. One under `closed/` takes no line.
2. Append the line, numbered one more than the last line in the file, with its body file when
   it has one.

### Close a thread

The opener's to do, or any addressed member's when the opener has gone quiet, once the thread
is complete. The closer's `done`, when the last line names the closer, is what completes it,
and the close sits in the same commit.

1. Move `open/m-<tid>.md` and its bodies, `open/m-<tid>-*.md`, to `closed/`.

## What is not here

- No inbox file. What is pending for a member is a query over `open/`, so a lost or stale inbox
  cannot disagree with the threads.
- No counter file per thread. The next number is read from the thread itself.
- No format version in the lines. The README's version is the rules', fields are additive,
  and a reader takes what is there.
- No second machine. The thread ids and line numbers are allocated under one clone's mutex, so
  two clones can mint the same id, a thread's from `threads` or a line's from the same last line.
  The rejected push catches it and the loser renumbers, which is why an id is final only once
  pushed. A second clone that never collides means member-scoped ids for threads and lines both,
  and that is the change it would take.
- No access control. Any member can modify or delete any file here. It works among friendly
  participants, and history is the only recourse.
- No commit per line. Under one clone the mutex is what keeps writes from interleaving, and a
  line's author and time are in the line, so a commit adds only the link to the session that
  wrote it. Committing batches lines, pushing backs them up, and the version commit is the one
  commit the rules require.
- No archive. `closed/` grows by a file per thread and its bodies, and git and `rg` carry that
  far past this family's traffic. The technique comes when it matters, a directory per year or a
  store outside the tree, and the ids, never reused, survive either.

## Versions

The title carries the rules' version, and the tree is always at that version: the commit that
bumps it edits this file and rewrites `open/` and `closed/` to the new shape in the same commit,
under the mutex, with every member's last push already in `main@origin`. History is never
rewritten, so a reader supports one shape, the one this file describes, and a tool that finds
the title behind it says so rather than parsing the past.

- v0.3.3: a commit is titled with the ids of the threads it touches, `m-3 m-4`, a close
  included, so the close form and the line-id form go. The first batch under v0.3.2 carried five
  lines across two threads and five ids read as noise, and a commit that closed two threads had
  no title form, iiac-perf's finding at `m-3-1`. The title is a convenience, never a store, and
  the diff says what the commit did in each thread.
- v0.3.2: a commit that closes a thread is titled `close m-<tid> <title>` whatever lines it
  carries, and a title that lists ids is for a batch that closes nothing. The first close under
  v0.3.1, `13a7d9f7`, carried six lines, and six ids read as noise where the close is the event.
- v0.3.1: no blank line under the heading, so line `<num>` is file line `<num>` plus two, closed
  threads move to `closed/` instead of being deleted, a commit may carry any number of actions,
  the close in the same commit as its last `done`, and a release may leave lines uncommitted, so
  the clean-working-copy guard is gone and a commit batches whatever the working copy holds. A
  member's own line, of either action, clears what was pending for them, so a reply needs no
  `done` after it, `done` is the empty reply, and `read` is retired, since a line that clears
  nothing has no place in a query over lines. From the `m-2` replies: addressed means the
  recipient field alone, a reply answers everything it clears, naming each, and `owner`'s times
  are UTC to the second. The migration restored `m-1` from history without its blank line, its
  surplus `done` marks still valid lines.
- v0.3.0, the cutover from v0.2.0's records and inboxes: every record was complete, so no
  thread carried over. `threads` was created at 0, `notices.md`, `topics/`, the inboxes,
  `README-old.md`, and the `.owner` copy of the mutex were deleted, and the draft became this
  file. The v0.2.0 tree is the tag `v0.2.0`, and `git log -S'<heading>'` finds a record.

## Specimen

`open/m-41.md`, opened by abc to def and ghi, answered by both, and complete: ghi's line at 1
and def's at 2 are above 0, the line naming them, and abc's `done` at 3 is above 1 and 2, the
lines naming abc. `threads` holds 41 or more. Line 2 has a body, `open/m-41-2.md` beside it,
shown after it.

```
# m-41 hello
- m-41-0 2026-09-09T16:00:00Z from abc to def,ghi hello
- m-41-1 2026-09-09T16:05:42Z from ghi to abc hi
- m-41-2 2026-09-09T16:09:12Z from def to abc [hey, and the cycle that answers it](m-41-2.md)
- m-41-3 2026-09-09T16:12:30Z from abc done
```

````
# m-41-2 hey, and the cycle that answers it

The cycle landed at
https://github.com/winksaville/def/blob/0123456789ab/TODO.md#feat-the-cycle.

## What changed

- one thing
- another, with the command that shows it:

  ```
  vc-x1 validate --fast
  ```
````

1. For each thread file, `open/m-<tid>.md` and never a body `open/m-<tid>-<num>.md`, find the
   `to` lines naming you. One numbered above your latest line in that file is pending, and the
   thread is the context to read it in.
2. Nothing pending, and `owner` shows no owner: consider doing a Fetch.

A tool may do the search. The rule is the file, and the tool is a convenience.

### Find a thread

Every thread is in the tree, under `open/` or `closed/`.

- Titles: `head -1 open/*.md closed/*.md`. Titles and openers: `head -2`.
- One thread: `cat open/m-<tid>.md` or `cat closed/m-<tid>.md`, `rg -w m-<tid>` for both and
  its bodies.
- A thread's commits, each titled with the thread ids it touched:
  `git log --oneline -- open/m-<tid>.md closed/m-<tid>.md`.

## Write Actions

Every write runs inside these guards, in order:

- `Read messages` first, so the write answers the traffic as it stands.
- Read `owner`: no other member has taken ownership.
- Any guard failing: show the user and ask how to proceed.
- Re-read `owner` before releasing, and a `take` after yours means stop and show both lines.
- A rejected push: work with the user to correct the situation.

Every write is an append: a thread file grows at its end, a body is a new file, and `threads` is
the one value that is overwritten. Nothing edits a line or a body once written.

1. Take ownership.
2. Do any number of the actions below, in any threads: open, write lines, close. Each line
   follows its own rule, and the mutex serializes the write, not the action.
3. Release ownership. A commit is optional for lines: the mutex serializes the writers and a
   line carries its author and time, so an uncommitted line is as visible and as final as a
   pushed one, and the working copy may hold lines from several takes. Who commits is the
   humans' call, the member closing a thread the default, and the commit takes the working copy
   whole, titled with the ids of the threads it touches, ascending, `m-3 m-4`, whatever it does
   in them, lines, bodies, or a close, since the diff says which and the title is a convenience,
   never a store. Push when connected, since the remote is the copy no session can lose and the
   target every sha-link needs. A version commit is never optional (see Versions).

### Fetch

1. Ask the user, unless their permission is standing.
2. `git fetch`, or `jj git fetch --ignore-working-copy`, since a bare jj command snapshots the
   working copy, and that is a write.

### Open a thread

1. Read `threads`, add one, write it back. That is the thread id.
2. Create `open/m-<tid>.md`: the heading and the opener's `to` line, numbered 0, with its body
   file when it has one.

### Write a line

Follows Read messages. A reply, a forward, or a `done`, each a line, and each clears its
author's pending on its own. A reply answers everything the lines it clears asked, naming each
by id, accepted or not, and what it does not accept is said to the asker, so they are pending
again and the exchange runs until both agree or the humans settle it. What a message asks for
is done in the author's own project's records, a Todo or a cycle, which outlive the thread, and
the reply links the outcome by sha-link.

1. The thread file exists under `open/`. One under `closed/` takes no line.
2. Append the line, numbered one more than the last line in the file, with its body file when
   it has one.

### Close a thread

The opener's to do, or any addressed member's when the opener has gone quiet, once the thread
is complete. The closer's `done`, when the last line names the closer, is what completes it,
and the close sits in the same commit.

1. Move `open/m-<tid>.md` and its bodies, `open/m-<tid>-*.md`, to `closed/`.

## What is not here

- No inbox file. What is pending for a member is a query over `open/`, so a lost or stale inbox
  cannot disagree with the threads.
- No counter file per thread. The next number is read from the thread itself.
- No format version in the lines. The README's version is the rules', fields are additive,
  and a reader takes what is there.
- No second machine. The thread ids and line numbers are allocated under one clone's mutex, so
  two clones can mint the same id, a thread's from `threads` or a line's from the same last line.
  The rejected push catches it and the loser renumbers, which is why an id is final only once
  pushed. A second clone that never collides means member-scoped ids for threads and lines both,
  and that is the change it would take.
- No access control. Any member can modify or delete any file here. It works among friendly
  participants, and history is the only recourse.
- No commit per line. Under one clone the mutex is what keeps writes from interleaving, and a
  line's author and time are in the line, so a commit adds only the link to the session that
  wrote it. Committing batches lines, pushing backs them up, and the version commit is the one
  commit the rules require.
- No archive. `closed/` grows by a file per thread and its bodies, and git and `rg` carry that
  far past this family's traffic. The technique comes when it matters, a directory per year or a
  store outside the tree, and the ids, never reused, survive either.

## Versions

The title carries the rules' version, and the tree is always at that version: the commit that
bumps it edits this file and rewrites `open/` and `closed/` to the new shape in the same commit,
under the mutex, with every member's last push already in `main@origin`. History is never
rewritten, so a reader supports one shape, the one this file describes, and a tool that finds
the title behind it says so rather than parsing the past.

- v0.3.3: a commit is titled with the ids of the threads it touches, `m-3 m-4`, a close
  included, so the close form and the line-id form go. The first batch under v0.3.2 carried five
  lines across two threads and five ids read as noise, and a commit that closed two threads had
  no title form, iiac-perf's finding at `m-3-1`. The title is a convenience, never a store, and
  the diff says what the commit did in each thread.
- v0.3.2: a commit that closes a thread is titled `close m-<tid> <title>` whatever lines it
  carries, and a title that lists ids is for a batch that closes nothing. The first close under
  v0.3.1, `13a7d9f7`, carried six lines, and six ids read as noise where the close is the event.
- v0.3.1: no blank line under the heading, so line `<num>` is file line `<num>` plus two, closed
  threads move to `closed/` instead of being deleted, a commit may carry any number of actions,
  the close in the same commit as its last `done`, and a release may leave lines uncommitted, so
  the clean-working-copy guard is gone and a commit batches whatever the working copy holds. A
  member's own line, of either action, clears what was pending for them, so a reply needs no
  `done` after it, `done` is the empty reply, and `read` is retired, since a line that clears
  nothing has no place in a query over lines. From the `m-2` replies: addressed means the
  recipient field alone, a reply answers everything it clears, naming each, and `owner`'s times

  file. The v0.2.0 tree is the tag `v0.2.0`, and `git log -S'<heading>'` finds a record.

### figures draws time per step against inner

A table of medians hides the period of 4 under the overhead's fall with `inner`, and its source
can be misread, as the period-of-4 entry's table and its thirty-run bullet were (wink,
2026-10-15, asking for a graph of all the data). A throwaway drawing of every run on the 7600X
`ccx` pair, `tmp/inner-raw.png` and `tmp/inner-overhead-off.png` on the 3900X, showed it at
once: the fixed collections agree, `sos-futex-spntfe` zigzags by `inner` modulo 4, random lengths
are smooth, and over 1-32 the runs split into two rates.

- `iiac-perf figures` learns the kind of figure, `--figure`, the block means its first, and
  panels that hold dots and a categorical colour and a legend as well as lines
- time per step against `inner`, every run a dot coloured by `inner` modulo 4, fixed runs as
  points and random runs as a line a run through their lengths
- the same with the harness overhead off, from `linear-regression`'s own arithmetic, so the
  figure and the command cannot disagree
- a random run's slope, one dot a run, to show the two rates
- the figures go into [random-inner.md](notes/random-inner.md) as committed SVGs drawn from
  `records/`, with the commands that redraw them

### The period of 4 in a can-sleep ring's level

A two-thread bench on a ring that can sleep reads low when `inner`, the steps timed back to back
in one sample, is a multiple of 4, and high when it is odd (wink, 2026-10-08, after the overnight
sessions on the landed names disagreed with the first session). The harness sizes `inner` by
itself in every run, so the level a bench reports depends on where that sizing lands.

156:## Cycle bookmarks: create and land
157-
158-The mechanics behind [Cycles run on a bookmark](../AGENTS.md#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark). That section
159-holds the rule and when it applies, and this one holds the commands
160-([why](rationale.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land)).
161-
162-**Create**, at the cycle's opening, with the bookmark named by the cycle title's slug (the anchor
163-algorithm in [Markdown anchor links](notes.md#markdown-anchor-links), so the block's title heading
164-and the bookmark derive from one bare title):
165-
166-- `jj git push --named <bookmark>=@- -R .` is the common case: it creates the bookmark at the last
167-  committed change and publishes it in one invocation.
168-- Any other revision works as the `=<rev>` right-hand side. When `<rev>` is not `@-`, follow with
169-  `jj new <rev> -R .` so the working copy actually sits on the new line. Otherwise the bookmark
170-  exists and the next commit lands somewhere else.
171-- `jj bookmark set <bookmark> -r <rev> -R .` creates it without publishing, for a line that is not
172-  ready to be seen.
173-
174-**Land**, once the close-out is approved: the sequence that makes the cycle permanent, begun by a
175-sync that found `main` unmoved ([Sync](../AGENTS.md#sync)). Every
176-`jj git push` in it is a push under [Approval per push](../AGENTS.md#before-any-push) and [Hard
177-stop after the final push](../AGENTS.md#at-rest-push-stop-squash-push), its own approval, the
178-closing words before the final invocation, silence after ([At
179-rest](../AGENTS.md#at-rest-push-stop-squash-push)):
180-
181-1. Restore the plain name, when the project renamed ([Dev artifact
182-   name](versioning.md#dev-artifact-name)): rename `<name>-dev` back to `<name>` in the manifest,
183-   `vc-x1 validate --fast` so the lockfile follows, and `jj squash` folds the edit into the closing
184-   (`@` sits directly above it).
185-2. Reshape per the recorded choice: trapezoid runs the [recipe below](#trapezoid-close-out-recipe),
186-   keep separate needs nothing. A single-step cycle has no choice recorded and its one commit lands

# Cycle model

A cycle's `## In Progress` block, shown as a specimen rather than a skeleton: the `config loader`
cycle, mid-run, with its opening landed and its first work rung current. Copy the shape, not the
words. The rules are in [The In Progress block](notes.md#the-in-progress-block).

One thing the specimen cannot show:

- a single-step cycle drops both bookends and all the steps are in the one commit: the ladder is one
  unlinked rung with the bare title, and there are no rung subsections under it ([Cycle
  shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)).

## In Progress

### refactor: extract config loader

#### Problem

Config parsing lives inside the CLI entry point, so every subcommand that wants a setting reaches
through `main` for it, and a test cannot load a config without building the CLI.

#### Solution

Move config loading into its own module with a single `load` entry point that the CLI and the tests
call alike.

#### Acceptance check

`cargo test` passes with a new test that loads a config from a fixture file without touching `main`,
and `vc-x1 config --validate` reports the same findings as before the move.

#### Deliberation

- one work rung, not two: the parser and the loader were going to be split first and moved second,
  but the move is what forces the split, so doing them together is fewer edits
- the acceptance check compares `config --validate` output rather than asserting on internals, so a
  later rename inside the module does not invalidate it

##### refactor: extract config loader opening

The cycle's setup commit: create and publish the bookmark, delete `## Closed`'s contents, move the
Todo entry into this block, and bump the version-of-record.

##### refactor: split loader from parser

Loading and parsing are one function, so the CLI cannot load without parsing and a test cannot parse
without a file on disk.

* The two jobs share one function and one error type.
  - `config/loader.rs` finds and reads the file, returning the text and its path, so a caller that
    only wants to know which file was read stops here.
  - `config/parser.rs` takes text and returns the schema, so a test hands it a string and never
    touches the filesystem.
    - the error type stays shared for now, since splitting it would change the messages
      `config --validate` prints and the acceptance check compares them
* `main` still reaches into the parse result by field.
  - `main` calls `config::load` and receives the schema, so the field access moves behind the module
    boundary and the CLI no longer knows the file's shape.

##### refactor: extract config loader closing

Closing out the cycle.

124-- **solution statement**: what will be done about it, broad. Provisional, and the close-out's commit
125-  body carries the final one
126-- **acceptance check**: the measure of "are you finished?", specific enough that a reader can run
127-  it. Not the per-commit validation, which asks whether the artifact still works. A changed check is
128-  one of the things the deliberation exists to justify
129-- **deliberation**: how the other five were decided, one bullet per decision. The bullet's lead
130-  names the decision and its sentence states it, and the sub-bullets carry the reasons, the
131-  alternatives weighed, and the costs accepted, so a reader can skim the decisions and read the
132-  reasons only where they doubt one. `_None._` when there was nothing to deliberate, which is a real
133-  answer
134-- **ladder**: one rung per step, `- [<title>][M]` plus `(current)` / `(done)`, with `[M]: #<slug>`
135-  in the file's `# References`. The markers stay when the block moves to `## Closed`. `<title>` is
136-  the rung's commit title, `<type>: <desc>` per
137-  [Conventional-commit shape](prose.md#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit), so a moved
138-  `## Todo` entry is retitled. The closing rung, `<cycle title> closing`, is linked like the rest
139-
140-The ladder heads the **rung subsections**, one per rung under it, the closing included, headed by
141-the rung's exact title, so the ladder is their index. Each opens at laddering with an abstract-sized
142-intent statement (the rung's problem and solution in a sentence or two) and completes at the rung's
143-landing with the conceptual delta: design points, consequences, deferrals, never a restatement of
144-the landed commit body. The closing rung's opens with the stub "Closing out the cycle." and
145-completes at close-out with what closing taught, in problem/solution form, or `_None._`.
146-
147-A rung is `- [<title>][M] (marker)` and carries no detail beyond that: the title links to the rung's
148-subsection. A step is identified by its title (prose.md's [Steps are named, not
149-numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)), so a title carries no number, no version, and no
150-SHA. The version-of-record still bumps for every rung and its suffix still encodes the stage, but
151-that encoding belongs to the manifest and appears nowhere in prose.

The last cycle's finished record, moved here whole by its closing commit and deleted by the next

### agent-files(adoption): v0.2.9

#### Problem

The family's set is at v0.2.9 and this repo carries v0.2.5, four proposals behind. vc-x1's m-11-0
asks us to adopt v0.2.9, which takes v0.2.6 to v0.2.8 with it and replaces m-9-0.

#### Solution

Copied vc-x1's set at `12a73d7135ab` over ours with `vc-x1 agent-files copy -c ../vc-x1`,
`custom.md` included, which brought `## Acquaint` and `## Sync`, a rung's step 0 sync, the
ladder below the Deliberation, a validation failure read before a rerun, `session-lock.md`, and
`custom.md`'s Fetch line, and recorded the new size, ten files and 1879 lines. The reply to m-11
and m-9 follows the landing.

#### Acceptance check

`vc-x1 agent-files diff -c ../vc-x1` exits zero.

Pass: `0 of 12 differ`, exit 0.

#### Deliberation

- Single-step: the copy is the whole of the work, with one straightforward step.
- `custom.md` comes with the set (`-c`), so the Fetch line comes too (wink, 2026-10-15).
  - The three members then hold one `custom.md`, and the next re-sync is a copy.
  - The line makes wink's standing permission of 2026-10-09 cover this project's Fetch.
- Nothing local is lost: our agent-files matched vc-x1's v0.2.5 at `fdc80c0` file for file
  before the copy.
- The opening's sync, step 1 under v0.2.9, was a `vc-x1 sync --scope=both --dry-run` before the
  bookmark, which found both `main`s up to date with origin.

- agent-files(adoption): v0.2.9 (done)

content.content:
## In Progress

A cycle's record has one home at a time, and while the cycle runs this is it. The block's
shape is the specimen in [cycle-model.md](agent-data/cycle-model.md), and the rules are in
[The In Progress block](agent-data/notes.md#the-in-progress-block).

### feat: fit, the cost of a step from samples of many lengths

#### Problem

A bench's level is a sample's time divided by `inner`, the steps timed back to back in it, and
that carries two things that are not the step (wink, 2026-10-08):

- A fixed cost per sample, about one clock read, is shared out over the steps and left in.
  `min-now` on the 7600X smt placement, `--inner` fixed at nine values from 10 to 42, fits
  `18.27 + 18.47 / inner` ns to within 0.004 ns at every value. At the 21 that auto-sizing picks
  the share is 0.88 ns, 4.8% of the level.
- The harness sizes `inner` from the step's own cost, so a faster bench carries a smaller share
  and two benches compared are not measured alike. About 0.05 ns of the 1 ns between one-thread
  `Single` and `Multi` on the 7600X is that.

Nothing in iiac-perf separates the step from the sample, and the working was done by hand in
`tmp/`.

#### Solution

A `fit` subcommand that reads records taken at several fixed `inner` values and fits a line
through sample time against `inner`. The slope is the cost of one step and the intercept the cost
of one sample with no steps in it. It shows its working, each `inner` beside the line's value, so
the arithmetic can be followed. The records it is written against are collected first, a sweep of
`--inner` on the 7600X, and committed.

#### Acceptance check

`iiac-perf-dev fit records/inner-sweep-7600x.jsonl` reports for `min-now` a slope within 0.01 ns
of 18.27 ns and an intercept within 0.5 ns of 18.4 ns, and for
`zcr-mpsc-v4-2t-single-sos-futex-spntfe` on the ccx pair a period of 4. A test fits points made
from a known line and recovers its slope and intercept.

#### Ladder

- [feat: fit, the cost of a step from samples of many lengths opening][85] (done)
- [docs: an inner sweep on the 7600X][86]
- [feat: a fit subcommand, a line through sample time against inner][87]
- [feat: fit, the cost of a step from samples of many lengths closing][88]

#### Deliberation

- the slope, not a subtraction: the step's cost is read off a fitted line and no measured frame
  is taken off a mean
  - a frame probed alone costs differently from one in place, so subtracting it can go wrong for
    a small step
  - a large `inner` shrinks the share and turns every bench into a burst bench

content.text:
You're right that I wasn't using `zDOING.md` / `zCLOSED.md`. But I was following the rules this repo actually has, so the real question is whether to adopt the new format before this cycle or after it.

**Why I didn't use it:** iiac-perf carries agent-files v0.2.9. That version still keeps the cycle record in `TODO.md > ## In Progress` and `## Closed`. Our rules say a session follows its own agent-files, and vc-x1's newer files bind us only once we adopt them. The only hint I'd seen was `m-10-4` linking vc-x1's `zCLOSED.md`, which I noticed but didn't act on. I haven't read `../vc-x1` itself, so I'm assuming the format is newer than v0.2.9.

**Where the cycle stands:** almost nothing has happened. The only action is the published `feat-figures-draws-time-per-step-against-inner` bookmark, which sits on `main` (`0b6b686`) with nothing on it yet. `TODO.md` still holds only the earlier continuation-note edit. Changing course costs almost nothing now.

**Options:**
1. **Adopt first (my recommendation).** Pause figures and run an adoption cycle to bring the new set in. Then reopen figures under `zDOING.md` / `zCLOSED.md`. Our rules make convention work its own cycle, so it shouldn't ride inside the figures cycle. The empty figures bookmark can be deleted and recreated later, or left alone.
2. **Figures first, adopt after.** Run this cycle under v0.2.9 as planned and adopt next. This is correct by our rules, but we'd write one more cycle record in a format we're about to drop.
3. **Use the new format now without adopting it.** I'd advise against this. It mixes two rule sets in one cycle, and nothing in our agent-files would describe the record it writes.

**Before choosing 1, one thing to check:** whether the new format is in the template payload (`../vc-x1-template`) or only in vc-x1's own copy. If it's only vc-x1's, it may still be an open proposal, and adopting it early would copy someone else's experiment. No message has asked us to adopt anything past v0.2.9. If it is in the payload, I'd still want to confirm vc-x1 considers it ready, either by a message on a new thread or by your say-so.

Once you choose, I'll read `../vc-x1` and the template payload to confirm the version and what changed.

The plain version: I followed this repo's own, older rules, which don't include the new files yet. Nothing on the figures cycle has really started, so the cleanest path is to adopt the new rules in their own small cycle first, provided they're settled rather than still a vc-x1 experiment.

`.jj/repo/config-id`, and `jj config set --repo` writes there, but `stacked_config` still reads
  the old `.jj/repo/config.toml`. So the remedy jj's own hint and this cycle's error name, `jj
  config set --repo snapshot.max-new-file-size`, would not reach vc-x1, nor any other per-repo
  setting.

#### Deliberation

- vc-x1 reads jj's per-repo config the way the `jj` command does, through jj-lib's
  `secure_config::SecureConfig`, in place of the old `.jj/repo/config.toml`.
  - In this cycle (wink, 2026-10-15), since the error's remedy is a per-repo setting and would
    not reach vc-x1 without it. Its own rung, being a fix of its own.
  - The read is `maybe_load_config`, which creates no entry for a repo without a `config-id`,
    where `load_config` would. It may migrate an old-style `.jj/repo/config.toml`, as the `jj`
    command would.
- `snapshot` returns a typed error naming the refused paths and sizes, with jj's two remedies, a
  `.gitignore` entry or a larger `snapshot.max-new-file-size`, iiac-perf's proposal.
  - Every caller fails with it, the read-only ones included. The `jj` command only warns, and a
    warning is what was missed. The cost accepted: a work-repo holding an unignored large file
    stops every vc-x1 verb until it is dealt with, and an acquaint's `sync --dry-run` reports it
    as a finding.
  - `commit_any_size` keeps calling `snapshot_with` directly, and keeps letting a file of any size
    in.
  - The files that fit are already snapshotted when the error returns, since
    `snapshot_working_copy` commits the snapshot operation first, and the message says so.
- The agent-repo's remedy is the user's to choose, never written by vc-x1 (wink, 2026-10-15).
  When a refused file is in an agent-repo, the error adds a third remedy: `jj config set --repo
  snapshot.max-new-file-size 0` in the agent-repo, 0 meaning no limit to vc-x1 and the `jj`
  command alike, or a larger value.
  - vc-x1 reads the limit through jj-lib's layered config, defaults, then the user's, then the
    repo's, so a repo's value overrides whatever the user's config sets, wink's being 20 MiB, in
    that repo alone. That is why it is not written unasked: it overrides a limit the user chose.
  - Weighed and left: `vc-x1 init` and `vc-x1 clone` writing it, first silently and then on a
    prompt or a flag. Push has already stopped when the error is seen, so nothing is lost while
    the user decides.
  - Weighed and left: push lifting the limit for the agent-repo itself. squash-push does not know
    which repo is the agent-repo, and the `jj` command would keep refusing.
- The tests set a limit in-process, never through `jj config set --repo`, which writes an entry
  under the user's config dir for every test repo.
  - Found at the work: the user's `~/.config/jj/repos` held 17,228 entries, 16,965 of them for
    test fixture repos long gone, each holding only the `trunk()` alias jj writes at a repo's
    creation, or this cycle's first test runs' 1 KiB limit. Removed at wink's go, 2026-10-15.
  - The push test writes a file just over whatever limit the user's config resolves to, and
    skips when there is none.
- iiac-perf's proposed check under Before any push, that the review shows the agent-repo carrying
  the session's transcript, is declined (wink, 2026-10-15), `m-10-2`: the error makes the refusal
  seen, at a push and at every other snapshot.
- A ladder (wink, 2026-10-15). It opened as one, became single-step when the agent-repo's limit
  was left to the user, and is one again with the per-repo config's rung, nothing having pushed
  but the bookmark.
- The cycle is titled for what the user and a caller get, wink's title at the opening's
  description review, in place of "fix: a snapshot no longer drops files the size limit refused".
  The bookmark keeps the first title's slug, being published and deleted at Land.

#### Solution

vc-x1 reads a repo's own jj config where jj has kept it since 0.37, through jj-lib's
`SecureConfig`. A snapshot that refuses a new file over `snapshot.max-new-file-size` returns a
`FilesTooLarge` error naming the files, their sizes, and the remedies, so every verb stops on it,
push before either repo commits. A refused file in an agent-repo adds the remedy of no limit in
that repo's own config, left for the user to choose.

#### Acceptance check

- A value set by `jj config set --repo` is what `RepoSession` reads, in a test. Passed,
  `repo_config_is_read_where_jj_keeps_it`.
- A new file over the limit makes `RepoSession::snapshot` return the typed error, naming the file
  and its size, and a refused file in an agent-repo adds the `jj config set --repo` remedy, in
  tests. Passed, `snapshot_fails_on_a_new_file_over_the_limit` and
  `snapshot_in_an_agent_repo_names_no_limit_as_a_remedy`.
- `vc-x1 push` with a new file over the limit in either repo fails before committing either repo,
  naming the file, in a test. Passed, `cli_push_stops_on_a_file_the_size_limit_refused`, which
  fails with the old `snapshot`.
- `vc-x1 validate` passes. Passed.

#### Ladder

- [fix: a snapshot failing is reported to the user and in Result opening][1] (done)
- [fix: vc-x1 reads jj's per-repo config][2] (done)
- [fix: snapshot fails on a file the size limit refused][3] (done)
- [fix: a snapshot failing is reported to the user and in Result closing][4] (done)

##### fix: a snapshot failing is reported to the user and in Result opening

The cycle's setup commit: create and publish the bookmark, write this block, bump the
version-of-record, and rename the package to its dev name.

##### fix: vc-x1 reads jj's per-repo config

vc-x1 reads a repo's config from `.jj/repo/config.toml`, where jj has not kept it since 0.37, so
every per-repo setting is lost to it. It reads it through jj-lib's `SecureConfig`, as jj does.

- The repo layer is its own function, given the user's config dir, so a test points it at a temp
  dir and the user's is never written. `stacked_config` passes `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` or
  `~/.config`, the dir it already read the user's own config from.
- `maybe_load_config`, never `load_config`: a read mints no `config-id` and no entry for a repo
  without one. It does migrate an old-style `.jj/repo/config.toml` on first read, as jj does, and
  jj's warnings, the migration's among them, are logged as warnings.
- The rng `SecureConfig` takes, to mint an id when migrating, comes from `rand` and
  `rand_chacha` at jj-lib's versions, seeded from the OS as jj-cli seeds it. jj-cli's
  `JJ_RANDOMNESS_SEED` override is left out, being a test hook of its own.
- The workspace layer, `.jj/workspace-config-id`, stays out, named as a deviation beside the
  command-line and `EnvBase` layers. No vc-x1 setting is per-workspace.

##### fix: snapshot fails on a file the size limit refused

`snapshot` drops the list of files the limit refused, so every verb proceeds without them and
push commits without a word. It returns a typed error naming them instead, with the remedies.

- `FilesTooLarge` carries the repo, the refused files with their sizes, the limit, and whether
  the repo is an agent-repo, so a caller can match on it, and its message is jj's hint adapted:
  a `.gitignore` entry, or `jj -R <repo> config set --repo snapshot.max-new-file-size
  <largest>`, the command that now reaches vc-x1 by the rung before. An agent-repo's adds `... 0`.
- Push stops at its first stage, the change check, before committing either repo, since the
  check snapshots, and squash-push, sync, and every other verb stop the same way.
- The limit's read is one function, `max_new_file_size`, its 0 read as no limit, shared by the
  snapshot and the error.
- The session tests set a 1 KiB limit in-process, on a `CommandArg` layer as `jj --config` sets
  one, and read trees with `--ignore-working-copy`, so the `jj` command's own limit takes no part.
- Push's test is a CLI test, `tests/cli_push.rs`: the binary runs in a `CliFixture` whose
  isolated home holds the jj config, the 1 KiB limit included, so the test owns its limit and its
  per-repo entries die with the fixture. It asserts no rollback ran in either repo, so push
  stopped before its first commit, and it fails with the old `snapshot`, checked by hand.
  - Weighed first and left: an in-crate test writing a sparse file one byte over the user's own

Where the agent was, for the agent that comes next. Ephemeral, never a record: read first, acted
on, and reset to `_None._` by the reader. Kept here by the trial and no longer in `TODO.md`,
where [Acquaint](AGENTS.md#acquaint) still says to look.

- The bookmark `feat-figures-draws-time-per-step-against-inner` is published at `0b6b686`, the
  opening of [figures draws time per step against
  inner](TODO.md#figures-draws-time-per-step-against-inner) paused before its first commit for the
  cycle that made this file. Its ladder is agreed (wink, 2026-10-16): the opening, `figures`
  learns `--figure` and panels with dots, a categorical colour and a legend, time per step against
  `inner`, the same with the harness overhead off, a random run's slope, the 7600X probe records
  into `records/`, the figures into `notes/random-inner.md`, and the closing. The opening moves
  the bookmark forward to `main`.
- Messages (2026-10-13): `tmp/m-9-0-draft.md`, the message to zc-ring-x1 carrying the v3 and v4
  notes, a new thread, is held for wink's review and not sent. Its name is stale, `m-9` being
  vc-x1's thread now, so it takes the next id when sent. It still has the old names and a `<sha>`
  placeholder. Hold it until the figures cycle says which of the v4 note's findings stand:
  `Single`'s check cost on the 7600X, which it was to carry, follows `inner` and is withdrawn.
- `tmp/runs-debug.patch` is wink's two debug prints in `src/runs.rs`, set aside at the closing so
  its commit did not carry them.
- The stopped sweep's one pass, 800 runs, five two-thread benches on `smt` and `ccx` at 16 of 24
  `inner` values, is `tmp/layout-7600x/partial-big-sweep-7600x.jsonl` on the 3900X, with the
  probes' records beside it, none committed. They go into `records/probes-7600x-20261008/` in the
  cycle of [figures draws time per step against
  inner](TODO.md#figures-draws-time-per-step-against-inner), with
  `tmp/next-cycle-data/probes-README.md` as its README, which says what each group is and the loop
  that took it, read back from the 2026-10-08 session. `lay-*-r` and `-s` are two invocations with
  address randomization off.
- The 7600X has `iiac-perf-dev` 0.28.24-2 in `~/.cargo/bin`, copied there for the random runs,
  beside the plain `iiac-perf` 0.28.23. The Pi 5 and the 3900X have no dev build of this cycle
  beyond the 3900X's own.
- The overnight sessions of 2026-10-08 on the landed names, five invocations of ten runs and one
  of fifty per host, `--run-sleep 100-200ms`, are in `tmp/session-<host>-20261008/` on the 3900X
  and not committed. `tmp/cmp3.py` compares them with the first session. The v4 note's tables are
  not rebuilt from them, held by [The period of
  4](TODO.md#the-period-of-4-in-a-can-sleep-rings-level).

its own block from [zDOING.md](zDOING.md) and this file's references with that block's, so the
last record stays here until the next one is finished. Earlier cycles are in each landmark

rule in the frozen [notes/chores/](notes/chores) and [notes/done.md](notes/done.md).

differ`, but kept the record in `TODO.md`, so the opening of the figures cycle was writing it in
the old place. Adopt vc-x1's three files now, before that cycle's first commit.

#### Deliberation

- A layout of project files, not an agent-files adoption: the trial lives in vc-x1's records, its
  agent-files still name `TODO.md`, and ours match them file for file.

    that makes it the rule.
- vc-x1's files are the model, copied and edited (wink, 2026-10-16): the intros as vc-x1 has

  the Deliberation, the Solution, the Acceptance check, and the Ladder.

  there, and its agreed ladder kept in a continuation note. Its opening moves the bookmark to

where the record lives, [notes/README.md](notes/README.md) and [notes/ops.md](notes/ops.md), say

  `TODO.md#in-progress`, or `TODO.md#closed`.

# Closed: the last cycle's record

The last finished cycle's record, whole. A cycle's closing replaces this file's `## Closed` with
its own block from [zDOING.md](zDOING.md) and this file's references with that block's, so the
last record stays here until the next one is finished. Earlier cycles are in each landmark
commit's copy of the record, in `TODO.md > ## Closed` before this file, and the cycles before the
rule in the frozen [notes/chores/](notes/chores) and [notes/done.md](notes/done.md).

## Closed

### docs: the cycle record moves to zDOING.md and zCLOSED.md

(wink, 2026-10-16) vc-x1 keeps its cycle record out of `TODO.md`: the running cycle and the
continuation notes in `zDOING.md`, the last finished cycle in `zCLOSED.md`, and `TODO.md` holding
what we might do and nothing else. iiac-perf carries the same agent-files, v0.2.9, `0 of 12
differ`, but kept the record in `TODO.md`, so the opening of the figures cycle was writing it in
the old place. Adopt vc-x1's three files now, before that cycle's first commit.

#### Deliberation

- A layout of project files, not an agent-files adoption: the trial lives in vc-x1's records, its
  agent-files still name `TODO.md`, and ours match them file for file.
  - So `zDOING.md` says it is a trial and names vc-x1's Todo entry, by sha-link, as the cycle
    that makes it the rule.
- vc-x1's files are the model, copied and edited (wink, 2026-10-16): the intros as vc-x1 has
  them, its trial note pointing at vc-x1's entry, and the block's order, the Todo as picked, then
  the Deliberation, the Solution, the Acceptance check, and the Ladder.
- The figures cycle pauses before its first commit, its bookmark published at `0b6b686` and left
  there, and its agreed ladder kept in a continuation note. Its opening moves the bookmark to
  `main`.
- `## Bugs`, a pointer to [bugs.md](notes/bugs.md), goes into `TODO.md`'s intro with the two new
  files, as vc-x1 did. `## Ideas` stays in `TODO.md`.
- The `agent-files(adoption): v0.2.9` record in `## Closed` is deleted, as an opening deletes it,
  and is in its landmark `0b6b686`.
- Single-step, with no dev rename: the change is to the records alone, and a rename made and
  restored in one commit does nothing.

#### Solution

`zDOING.md` takes `## Continuation notes` and `## In Progress` from `TODO.md`, and `zCLOSED.md`
takes `## Closed`, each with vc-x1's intro. `TODO.md` keeps `## Waiting`, `## Todo`, `## Ideas`,
and its references, and its intro names the two files and `notes/bugs.md`. The notes that said
where the record lives, [notes/README.md](notes/README.md) and [notes/ops.md](notes/ops.md), say
so now.

#### Acceptance check

- `vc-x1 agent-files diff -c ../vc-x1` reports `0 of 12 differ`.
- The headings of `zDOING.md` and `zCLOSED.md` match vc-x1's, and `TODO.md`'s level-two headings
  are `## Waiting`, `## Todo`, and `## Ideas`.
- No file outside the agent-files and the frozen history links to `TODO.md#continuation-notes`,
  `TODO.md#in-progress`, or `TODO.md#closed`.

#### Ladder

- docs: the cycle record moves to zDOING.md and zCLOSED.md (current)

content.text:
It already is single-step: one commit, version `0.28.26`, no opening or closing rungs. So the question is only the title. I'd keep `chore`, but I'd avoid naming v0.2.9 in it.

**Why not "v0.2.9 cycle-rules":**
- We adopted the v0.2.9 rules last cycle, `agent-files(adoption): v0.2.9` at `0b6b686`. `vc-x1 agent-files diff` confirms `0 of 12 differ`.
- The v0.2.9 rules still put the record in `TODO.md > ## In Progress`. The `zDOING.md` / `zCLOSED.md` split is vc-x1's trial layered on top, which its own `zDOING.md` says is "a trial".
- So a title saying "v0.2.9" tells another member they're behind on the agent-files when they aren't. It also stops being accurate once vc-x1's cycle turns the trial into a rule, probably in a later version.

**What I'd suggest instead**, if you want it to read as a model others can follow:
- `chore: adopt vc-x1's cycle-record files` names the source and the thing adopted, so `git log --grep` finds it as the adoption.
- `chore: the cycle record moves to zDOING.md and zCLOSED.md` matches the wording of vc-x1's own Todo entry, so the two cycles read as a pair.

I lean toward the first, since "adopt" is the word another member would search for.

**To make it work as a model,** the record could carry a short recipe under its Solution, five steps another member repeats:
1. Copy vc-x1's `zDOING.md` and `zCLOSED.md`.
2. Move `## Continuation notes` and `## In Progress` into `zDOING.md`, and `## Closed` into `zCLOSED.md`.
3. Turn `## Bugs` into a pointer in `TODO.md`'s intro.
4. Repoint the notes that say where the record lives.
5. Check headings and links the way this cycle's acceptance check does.

After it lands, a line to zc-ring-x1 could link to the landmark as the model. That fits with the `tmp/m-9-0-draft.md` thread we're already holding for them.

The plain version: it's already single-step, so only the title changes. Naming v0.2.9 would mislead, because we already have v0.2.9 and this layout isn't part of it. I'd title it `chore: adopt vc-x1's cycle-record files` and add a short recipe so others can copy it.

# Commit model

Two commit bodies from the `config loader` cycle in [cycle-model.md](cycle-model.md), shown as
specimens rather than a skeleton: a work rung's body and a bookend's. Copy the shape, not the
words. The rules are in [Commit-body form](prose.md#commit-body-form).

## A work rung

Title: `refactor: split loader from parser`

```
Config loading and parsing are one function, so the CLI cannot load a
config without parsing it and a test cannot parse one without a file on
disk. The move into its own module is what forces the split.

* The two jobs share one function and one error type.
  - `config::loader` finds and reads the file and returns the text with
    its path, so a caller that only wants to know which file was read
    stops there.
  - `config::parser` takes text and returns the schema, so a test hands
    it a string and never touches the filesystem.
* `main` still reaches into the parse result by field.
  - `main` calls `config::load` and receives the schema, so the field
    access moves behind the module boundary and the CLI no longer knows
    the file's shape.
```

The intro states this commit's problem and defines "split", the word the title assumes. Each `*`
is one facet of it, each `-` under a `*` answers that facet, and nothing names a file that the
diff already lists.

## A bookend

Title: `refactor: extract config loader opening`

```
Opens the cycle "refactor: extract config loader". Its record is the
In Progress block in TODO.md.
```

A bookend resolves no problem of its own, so its body is the intro paragraph alone, naming the
cycle by its title and pointing at its record. The closing's body is the same shape with "Closes".
